item.stem:
This map shows city blocks with a delivery truck at one corner.

[Image: Map of city blocks with a delivery truck at corner X]

The driver of the delivery truck starts at corner X. He goes 3 blocks east and 2 blocks north to get to the school. On what corner is the school located?
item.figure_description: A street map showing a grid of 5 columns and 4 rows of rectangular blocks separated by streets. To the left is a compass rose with arrows indicating North pointing up and East pointing right. At the bottom-left corner of the bottom-left block (column 1, row 4 from top) is an illustration of a delivery truck, with the corner labeled 'X'. Five intersections are labeled with letters: 'A' is at the intersection between columns 2 and 3 and rows 2 and 3; 'B' is at the intersection between columns 3 and 4 and rows 2 and 3; 'C' is at the intersection between columns 4 and 5 and rows 2 and 3; 'D' is at the intersection between columns 2 and 3 and rows 1 and 2; 'E' is at the intersection between columns 3 and 4 and rows 1 and 2.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
For this item, you have been given a cardboard ruler. If you do not have the cardboard ruler raise your hand. Use the map below and your ruler to answer this set of questions.

Marytown is a new town. The people of Marytown are planning their new town. They decided to put the town hall halfway between the lake and the forest, as shown on the map below. They made their measurements from the X's.

Marytown

[Image: Map of Marytown]

Add a park, a library, and a school to the map of Marytown using the following information.

C. The school should be halfway between the park and the library. On the map, mark with an X where you would put the school and write school below the X.

descriptors: School equidistant from park and library, X to X, measures to differ no more than 4mm
School is not equidistant (+/- 2 mm) from park and library
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: Park, library, and school need not to be in a straight line.
reference_items.figure_description:
A map of Marytown enclosed in an irregular rectangular border.
Near the top right inside the border, text states: "Scale: 1 cm represents 100 meters".
In the upper-left quadrant is a forest represented by a cluster of pine trees, with an "X" mark below it labeled "Forest".
Near the center of the map is an "X" mark labeled "Town Hall" below it.
In the lower-right quadrant is an outlined body of water with wavy horizontal lines inside, with an "X" mark directly above it labeled "Lake".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

One centimeter on the map represents 8 kilometers on the land.

About how far apart are Oxford and Smithville on the land?

A thick curved line labeled 'Indian River' runs diagonally from the bottom-left edge up toward the top-right edge. Roads (thin lines) connect the towns across the map. Oxford is located in the upper-middle area, Hatboro is to the west, and Smithville is to the southeast. In the lower-right corner is a scale box displaying a line segment with vertical end ticks, labeled '1 cm = 8 km' below it.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
This figure will be turned to a different position.

[Image: A 3D figure made of cubes]

Which of these could be the figure after it is turned?
reference_items.figure_description: The initial figure is a solid composed of 5 cubes: 4 cubes form an upright T-shape (a horizontal row of 3 cubes at the bottom, and 1 cube centered on top of the middle cube), and a 5th cube is attached to the back face of the leftmost cube of the bottom row. Option A shows an upside-down T-shape (a horizontal row of 3 cubes at the top with 1 cube centered below the middle cube) with a 5th cube attached to the back face of the rightmost cube. Option B shows an upright T-shape with a 5th cube attached to the back face of the rightmost cube. Option C shows an upright T-shape with a 5th cube attached to the front face of the middle bottom cube. Option D shows a vertical column of 3 cubes with 2 cubes extending to the right and backward from the middle cube.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
